The timer is cleared in finally. On success the command prints 'Model catalogs refreshed'; error handling prints the error and sets exitCode=1. The target cannot combine with self/extensions/all/individual package targets, as enforced before runtime creation.

The command-path test asserts exact auth/models paths, no network during create, explicit forced network permission during refresh, shared AbortSignal and early rejection of conflicting targets. General catalog publication, provider-specific data and cancellation semantics are owned by AI-002/AUTH; this entry specifies only the CLI boundary and its ordering.
entries.interfaces: update --models; ModelRuntime.create({authPath,modelsPath,allowModelNetwork:false,signal}); runtime.refresh({allowNetwork:true,force:true,signal}); 15000 ms cooperative abort timer; success message and command failure status.
entries.dependency_text: AI-002 owns ModelRuntime catalog lifecycle, network permissions, publication and cancellation. SET-001 supplies agent paths. AUTH-032 is a different startup helper and is intentionally not used as the generic refresh dependency.
entries.rust: Native self-update parser accepts only help/force/build and the inspected app update route delegates to it. It exposes no --models target that constructs a local catalog runtime then explicitly enables a forced refresh (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/updates.rs:522-551; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/app.rs:136-172). Native model/provider catalogs exist elsewhere and are credited under AI/AUTH, but that does not implement this command.
entries.port: Add the dedicated model-refresh route above the native self-update parser and call the AI-002 runtime with separate create/refresh network permissions. Keep project package trust/settings out of this branch. Aggregate errors and propagate cooperative cancellation accurately. Future tests should prove no package/self-update operation occurs, conflicting targets fail before runtime creation, the deadline signal reaches both stages and partial provider failures do not print success.
entries.priority_reason: Users need an explicit catalog refresh independent of package or binary updates, with clear network authority and failure reporting.

entries.title: Self-update planning, global command selection and extension-before-self sequencing
entries.what: TS self-update asks for an exact target release and derives a platform/install-method command from global settings. Combined updates complete extension updates first and never claim self-update success after a command failure.
entries.mechanism:
Self-update checks the target release before deciding whether to run an installer. When extensions and self are both selected, extension updates finish first; a failure stops the later self-update stage.

getSelfUpdatePlan calls getLatestRelease(VERSION), wraps lookup failure and rejects missing metadata. It takes the returned packageName when available or the current PACKAGE_NAME, builds the exact '<package>@<version>' install spec, and runs when forced, when the package name changed or when the version is newer. Otherwise it reports already up to date. Explicit self-update still checks when automatic version checking is disabled; the version-check helper owns that distinction. A forced update still uses the checked version, not an unqualified latest install (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/package-manager-cli.ts:493-520; ice:packages/coding-agent/test/package-command-paths.test.ts:492-615).

The handler reads npmCommand from global settings only. Install-method/command derivation is SET-002. Windows permits only npm/pnpm self-update methods; unavailable methods print a manual fallback. Before an npm update on Windows it invokes cleanup and loaded-native-module quarantine helpers (MISC-002). Steps run sequentially with structured argv and inherited stdio, waiting for close; spawn, nonzero exit or signal errors fail the operation. A package rename can execute uninstall-old then install-new; failure of the second step does not reinstall the old package. Tests explicitly assert this nontransactional sequence and failure status (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/package-manager-cli.ts:521-562; ice:packages/coding-agent/test/package-command-paths.test.ts:617-769).

An optional release note is trimmed and rendered as Markdown at at least 20 columns (stdout width or fallback 80), with plain-text fallback if rendering fails. A pnpm failure adds the metadata/store-prune hint and manual command guidance. Success reports previous and target version only after every command step succeeds. The default no-target update selects self and prints that extension updates were skipped; --all or self+extensions first awaits the package update path, then runs this plan (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/package-manager-cli.ts:442-492; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/package-manager-cli.ts:788-905).

Remote metadata validation and package-migration trust are MISC-001, not reimplemented here. Native self-update has a different artifact-staging/activation architecture that should be retained rather than replaced with an npm-only strategy.
entries.interfaces: SelfUpdatePlan includes checked target version/package install spec, note and shouldRun decision. SelfUpdateCommand supplies method, ordered steps and manual command. --force affects version comparison but does not bypass the TS release lookup. Global npmCommand only; Windows quarantine is an invocation prerequisite, not proof of native executable activation.
entries.dependency_text: CLI-027 supplies extension updates for combined targets; SET-002 chooses safe commands/install method; MISC-001 validates release metadata/comparison and MISC-002 owns loaded-DLL quarantine/cleanup. Native activation counterparts are preserved in CLI-043–046.
entries.rust: Native update checks crates.io, stages a Cargo-built or verified prebuilt executable, validates it and activates it directly or through a detached Windows helper. It does not use the TS package-name migration/global npmCommand plan, --self/--extensions target matrix or note rendering. Native --force --build can skip metadata and Cargo build does not pin the looked-up version, unlike the TS exact spec (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/updates.rs:668-786; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/updates.rs:819-895). Native safeguards and defects are specified separately.
entries.port: Unify user-visible update target sequencing while retaining the native staged binary updater. Reuse MISC-001 for any TS-compatible update-service metadata and SET-002/MISC-002 only when updating a JS installation. Never let project npmCommand affect self-update. Report partial package-name migration accurately and choose a recovery strategy rather than claiming current TS rollback. Future checks should cover current forced version, renamed package install failure, extensions failure before self, unsupported Windows methods, close/signal errors and Markdown fallback.
entries.priority_reason: Self-update can replace the running installation; exact target selection, trusted command scope and honest failure sequencing are essential.

entries.title: Native project package links: preserve Cargo workflow and close name-containment holes
entries.what: Rust already supports project-local Cargo package link/list/update/unlink commands. This native-only workflow should remain available, but its permissive project-name validator and unvalidated registry names can escape the intended package-name directory.
entries.mechanism:
TS local resource installation records an existing source path without copying it. Rust's project link command instead builds a Cargo dynamic library and installs a copied artifact under the project, so its filesystem mutation boundary must be evaluated independently.

Native 'package link' accepts --path, --package/-P, --name or one positional display name, --debug, --locked and --force/-f. It resolves the source against cwd, runs cargo metadata --format-version 1 --no-deps, selects the requested Cargo package or a unique cdylib candidate (preferring the canonical source-containing manifest where unambiguous), then builds using JSON compiler-artifact messages and release by default. The build occurs before the existing target/no-force check. It selects a dynamic library artifact and targets cwd/.ice/packages/<name>/extensions. Force removes the old target before copying through a fixed adjacent temporary filename and rename. Registry parsing/updating occurs after artifact activation, so a corrupt registry or later write failure can leave changed payload without matching metadata (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/packages.rs:48-190; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/packages.rs:468-605).

The project registry is {packages:[{name,version,source,cargo_package,artifacts?}]} with missing artifacts defaulting empty. Writes use .packages.json.tmp then rename, without the global installer's mutation lock or multi-file rollback. List reads only this project registry. Update strictly reads both project and global registries before rebuilding; it relinks selected project records with force, then invokes the current executable's native install command for eligible global records. It preserves custom GitHub/prebuilt versus --build backend, excludes local-source global entries, continues after individual failures and returns aggregate failure. Project --locked/debug affect Cargo rebuilds, not every global installer invocation. Unlink validates one name, requires a matching record, removes its directory before rewriting the registry, and does not have rollback (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/packages.rs:192-467).

Source-proven containment defect: valid_name accepts any nonempty ASCII alphanumeric/dash/underscore/dot sequence, including '.' and '..'. Direct app dispatch reaches package::run; a supplied --name '..' passes validation. Given a valid source/build, joining that name can direct the artifact into cwd/.ice/extensions and persist '..' if the registry write succeeds. Unlink '..' then requires that registry record and calls remove_dir_all on cwd/.ice/packages/.. before updating metadata. The audit did not execute this or establish OS-specific deletion effects for a terminal parent component. Cargo-derived selected.name uses the same validator, but Cargo's own permitted-name constraints were not independently audited. Parsed registry names have no semantic revalidation, and project_package_dirs directly joins registry name/kind, so malformed stored names affect discovery as well (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/packages.rs:123-166; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/packages.rs:388-421; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/packages.rs:573-626).

Inline tests cover backend selection, custom repositories, continuing after failures and corrupt-global-registry early abort. The name test rejects slash traversal and empty names but does not cover '.'/'..'. All tests were read only. Native package linking copies the library, not all skills/prompts/themes; the directory-discovery interface can expose those kinds only when corresponding directories exist through other means.
entries.interfaces: Native commands package link/list/update/unlink; .ice/packages/<name>/extensions; .ice/packages.json and fixed .packages.json.tmp; Cargo package/display-name split. Source-only preconditions for the defect are a directly supplied dot name plus successful metadata/build/link persistence, or an existing matching malformed registry record for unlink.
entries.dependency_text: No cross-area prerequisite is required to correct the native path boundary. New npm/Git/local compatibility sources remain CLI-020–033 and must not be conflated with this Cargo workflow.
entries.rust: The native implementation is substantial and directly reachable at app.rs:157. Its global installer has stricter non-dot crate names and transactional artifact handling; those safeguards do not automatically apply to project package link/unlink. The exact difference is unchecked dot/registry-name containment and nontransactional project mutation, not absence of all package management. Native source hashes and all inline tests are recorded in cli-packaging-supplement-source-review.json.
entries.port: Keep native Cargo link/update/list/unlink, but reject '.'/'..' and any non-single-component name at every direct and registry-derived boundary. Validate a target as a strict descendant of the intended package root before copy/removal/discovery, and revalidate registry names before using them. Treat symlink/canonical containment and existing project data compatibility explicitly. Reuse the global mutation staging/locking pattern where practical so registry corruption is detected before payload activation and failed force replacement can recover. The estimated change covers this boundary/ordering correction, not reimplementation of Cargo link or TS source backends. Future source-driven checks should cover dot names, corrupted/untrusted registries, symlinked destinations and failure between payload/registry updates without running destructive operations during this audit.
entries.priority_reason: A user-controlled package name reaches recursive removal and artifact paths without enforcing the intended project package boundary.

entries.title: Native Cargo artifact installation, ownership locking and rollback to preserve
entries.what: The Rust package installer already provides a native Cargo/prebuilt artifact registry with ownership checks, locked mutations and rollback. These capabilities are distinct from TS npm/Git resource packages and should be retained when compatibility backends are added.
entries.mechanism:
TS resource-package installation delegates to npm-family or Git commands and then edits settings. Rust's global installer instead owns a set of native library artifacts and updates that set together with its registry under a lock.

Native run_async reads the registry strictly before work. --build or --path uses a blocking Cargo path; otherwise online prebuilt installation is the default, with no automatic Cargo fallback after prebuilt failure. The parser accepts crate name, --version/-V, --path, --locked, --force/-f, --build and --github with mutually exclusive combinations. Local path can infer the selected crate via canonical manifest metadata. Global crate names allow ASCII alphanumeric/dash/underscore and reject dot components (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/install.rs:155-398; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/install.rs:1075-1362).

Cargo installation creates a temporary build workspace and dependency alias, performs fetch/metadata, identifies the selected package and requires a cdylib, builds release artifacts and finds platform dynamic libraries (including .pyd in the artifact matcher). Version policy is semver precedence: force or no current record permits installation, greater versions upgrade, equal versions skip, and downgrade/invalid version comparison errors unless force bypasses that comparison. The Cargo command inherits stdio and forwards locked/offline where applicable; there is no package-build cancellation/deadline contract in this path.

Mutation takes an exclusive fs2 try-lock at native-packages.lock, rereads the registry and rechecks the version under lock. Artifact inputs must be regular nonsymlink files with flat UTF-8 dynamic-library filenames, unique by the platform's identity rule (case-insensitive on Windows). Another package's owned filename conflicts even with force. Unowned existing target files require force. The installer stages create_new adjacent UUID files, copies/syncs contents and preserves permissions, backs up affected regular nonsymlink files, activates replacements and writes the sorted registry last. On failure it reverses activations/backups; rollback errors are surfaced and backup cleanup failures warn. This is a multi-file rollback protocol, not a crash-atomic filesystem transaction or parent-directory fsync guarantee (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/install.rs:484-1074).

Uninstall uses the same lock and strict registry. Explicit recorded artifacts are authoritative; legacy records use bounded normalized stem matching. It scans dynamic library files only, removes transactionally with the remaining sorted registry, and removes the registry when last package is gone. A not-installed crate prints a message and exits successfully. Startup discovery uses best-effort registry reading, unlike fail-closed mutation. Inline tests cover corrupt registry, forced upgrades, unowned/foreign-owned collisions, multiple artifact replacement, rollback, legacy provenance and uninstallation; they were read, not run.
entries.interfaces: InstalledNativePackage includes name, version, optional source, optional prebuilt provenance and optional artifacts. Native package registry, native-packages.lock and platform library directory are independent from TS settings packages arrays. Registry version/artifact ownership and force are native protocol surfaces.
entries.dependency_text: This is a preservation entry. New source parsing/resource caches are separately estimated in CLI-020–033; native prebuilt validation is CLI-041. No missing transaction implementation is inferred.
entries.rust: All described native transaction behavior is present in install.rs and its inline tests. TS npm/Git command delegation does not provide this same artifact-level ownership transaction. The absence of npm/Git resource backends remains a gap elsewhere; it must not be used to erase or double-count the native installer.
entries.port: Retain the Cargo backend, strict mutation registry, artifact ownership checks, lock, staging and rollback when adding resource-package commands. Do not replace them with TS's weaker payload-then-settings ordering. Keep backend-specific registries separate and expose native versus resource-package identities explicitly in the command facade. No new Rust implementation is required for this retained capability; size is zero and compatibility work is counted in the owning source/CLI entries.
entries.priority_reason: Preservation-only native capability; existing transactional implementation should not be counted as missing port work.

entries.title: Verified native extension prebuilt distribution and publisher provenance to preserve
entries.what: Rust can install verified prebuilt native extensions from publisher releases without building Cargo source. The protocol validates manifest identity, platform/ABI and archive/library integrity before handing artifacts to the transactional installer.
entries.mechanism:
TS npm/Git packages use their external package manager or checkout transport. Native prebuilt extensions instead follow a bounded release-manifest protocol and retain publisher provenance for later updates.

The native host target set is Windows x86_64 MSVC, Linux x86_64/aarch64 GNU and macOS x86_64/aarch64; unsupported targets must use the build path. Repository canonicalization accepts owner/repo or HTTPS GitHub forms (including supported repository subpaths), trims git+/.git/trailing syntax and lowercases owner/repository, rejecting auth, ports and invalid/dot components. crates.io resolution normalizes '-'/'_' identity, chooses the highest non-yanked stable version when unspecified and requires an exact requested non-yanked version when specified. Explicit --github plus version can bypass crates.io; explicit repository without version chooses the highest stable '<name>-v<version>' tag. A changed publisher must be explicit rather than silently switching an existing installation (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/prebuilt_extensions.rs:1-424).

The ice-extension.json schema must be version 1 with matching package/version/tag/repository, 40-character lower-case source commit, valid SDK semver, matching plugin ABI, exact host target and a zip/tar.gz artifact. Archive URL must be HTTPS on the same GitHub repository/tag, with the expected release asset path and no auth/port/query/fragment. Library filename is flat, ASCII-constrained and platform-suffixed. SHA-256 fields are 64 lower-case hex characters. Metadata is bounded at 8 MiB, manifest at 256 KiB, archive at 256 MiB, library at 128 MiB and entries at 128; archive size must be positive and match the manifest (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/prebuilt_extensions.rs:425-803).

HTTP metadata uses a 15-second client timeout and archive work 180 seconds. Limited-body reading checks both declared content length and streamed bytes. ZIP/tar.gz extraction never blindly unpacks paths: it rejects traversal, absolute/backslash/colon forms, links and special entries, counts entries and expanded sizes, and extracts the single declared library once. It verifies archive and extracted-library hashes. Object validation checks PE64 AMD64 DLL, ELF64 little-endian shared-object/architecture, or Mach-O64 little-endian dylib/CPU type without executing the library. Exported runtime ABI is still checked when loading later; manifest SDK/ABI checks do not prove every exported function is correct.

The persisted provenance records repository, target, manifest/source/SDK/ABI/archive/library hashes and whether the repository was custom. Updates preserve the chosen backend/publisher and validate compatibility for a newer release before offering it. An unchanged/older version can be returned without fetching a new target manifest. Installation delegates to CLI-040's artifact transaction. All inline tests and local-HTTP fixtures were read, including platform/object validation, publisher/tag scoping, archive bounds and explicit unpublished package installation; none ran.
entries.interfaces: ice-extension.json schema 1; '<name>-v<version>' release tag; native artifact/provenance registry; --github, --version, --build and --force. Supported target triples and byte/entry limits are protocol constraints. No npm resource manifest or general Git checkout semantics are implied.
entries.dependency_text: The verified output library is activated through the existing locked transaction. Runtime plugin loading/ABI export checks remain EXT-owned. This retained protocol is also reused by CLI prebuilt self-update helpers, with a distinct repository-case defect in CLI-045.
entries.rust: The implementation and inline tests are fully present in prebuilt_extensions.rs. It is a useful native-only capability absent from TS's npm/Git package transport. The helper canonicalization is internally consistent for its canonical repository inputs; the separate CLI prebuilt caller's mixed-case constant is not proof that every extension prebuilt install is broken.
entries.port: Preserve the bounded manifest/archive protocol, publisher continuity, provenance and object validation while adding TS resource backends. Keep verification before activation and runtime ABI loading after it. No new Rust implementation is estimated for this retained capability. Do not loosen archive/path/hash limits to make TS package naming fit, and do not treat downloaded native libraries as equivalent to JS package directories.
entries.priority_reason: Preservation-only verified native distribution; it should remain intact and contributes no missing-port LOC.

entries.title: Native startup update cache, per-entry freshness and backend-aware notices to preserve
entries.what: Native startup checks already use bounded concurrency, per-entry metadata freshness and backend-aware update notices. Resource-package checks can be added without replacing those native reliability properties.
entries.mechanism:
TS package update discovery probes installed npm/Git packages and suppresses metadata errors. Native startup additionally retains recent successful version metadata and uses it only for transient lookup failures.

check_startup ignores its cwd parameter for native package selection; it checks the global native registry and the CLI. ICE_OFFLINE or the presence of ICE_DISABLE_UPDATE_CHECK, even an empty value, disables remote checks while still consuming self-update status warnings. The startup HTTP client has a 1800 ms request timeout and the native user-agent configuration. Extension checks use buffer_unordered with concurrency four; the CLI version check runs concurrently outside that four-item pool. Locally sourced global native packages are excluded (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/updates.rs:120-253).

Registry results distinguish Found(version), Missing for HTTP 404/410, and Transient for other failures including throttling, timeouts and malformed metadata. Cached metadata is reused only on Transient and only when checkedAt>0 with age between zero and six hours inclusive. Fallback does not renew freshness. Missing removes the old result. The cache file is update-check.json with legacy checkedAt plus newer per-entry timestamps; cache updates lock, reread and merge sections before best-effort atomic writing so concurrent CLI/native results do not clobber each other. There is no claim that all cached metadata is freshly network-verified (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/updates.rs:254-357; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/updates.rs:445-493).

Cargo entries use a crate-name cache identity; prebuilt entries include the distribution backend, repository/name and target to avoid cross-publisher/platform reuse. Before reporting, the code rereads the installed registry and checks semver 'newer than', not mere string inequality. Notice commands preserve the appropriate native update/install backend and custom repository. CLI notices use 'ice update'. These semantics differ from TS npm/Git inequality probes and are native capabilities to preserve, not a missing one-to-one algorithm (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/updates.rs:358-419; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/updates.rs:474-521).

Explicit offline self-update uses cached_latest_ice without this startup six-hour freshness check; that separate informational path is CLI-043. Full inline tests cover transient versus missing fallback, freshness boundaries, cache merging, publisher/platform keys, worker bounds and notice behavior. No network or startup check ran during this audit.
entries.interfaces: ICE_DISABLE_UPDATE_CHECK presence semantics; ICE_OFFLINE native gate; update-check.json cache; UpdateReport notices/warnings; Found/Missing/Transient classification; six-hour fallback, 1800 ms requests and concurrency four plus independent CLI request. TS ICE_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK/update-service semantics remain MISC-001.
entries.dependency_text: Prebuilt provenance and compatibility lookup supply backend-aware identities. New npm/Git discovery is separately owned/estimated by CLI-028; TS release HTTP metadata is MISC-001.
entries.rust: All described native caching and notice behavior is present in updates.rs. It is stronger/different than the package manager's uncached npm/Git notice probes. The missing source backends and explicit CLI target grammar are separately captured, and should not be double-counted as absent caching infrastructure.
entries.port: Retain native result classification, freshness, merge locking and publisher-aware keys. Add resource-package notices through explicit backend-tagged records and shared presentation only after CLI-028 exists. Preserve the distinction between automatic native disable flags and TS explicit update-service behavior. No replacement implementation is required for this retained capability; size is zero.
entries.priority_reason: Preservation-only native reliability behavior; resource-package notice work is already counted elsewhere.

entries.title: Native self-update source selection, isolated builds and already-staged retry defect
entries.what: Native self-update prepares a new executable in an isolated staging directory and selects Cargo-build versus prebuilt acquisition. Its already-staged branch does not actually suppress all duplicate work claimed by the surrounding comments.
entries.mechanism:
TS self-update selects an exact checked package version and runs package-manager steps. Rust prepares a native executable, with separate metadata lookup, staged-version selection and platform activation.

Native arguments accept help, force and build after the app's offline normalization; other target flags produce usage code 2. Offline self-update consumes existing status/artifact information, reports a last-known cached version and exits without downloading/building. That informational cached version is not subject to the startup six-hour freshness test. Online lookup runs through a separate Tokio thread/runtime with a 15-second request timeout and can fall back to fresh cached metadata marked verified=false. The prebuilt path requires a known target version but does not reject that fallback solely because verified is false; artifact manifest/hash validation still occurs later (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/updates.rs:522-606; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/updates.rs:668-818).

When --force --build is selected, metadata lookup can be skipped. Cargo preparation uses a private command directory under the agent home instead of the project cwd, removes the four Rust compiler wrapper/workspace wrapper environment overrides in the implementation, validates configured CARGO_HOME as absolute and outside the project (including missing-path canonicalization), and runs cargo install --root <staging> ice-cli --locked --force --quiet. It does not pass the previously looked-up version with --version. The final binary validation enforces acceptable identity/version; it does not make that build an exact replay of the queried release. Cargo build duration is not bounded by the 15-second metadata timer (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/updates.rs:819-1050).

Source-proven staged-selection defect: run_self_update calls pending_staged_version, whose staged_pending_version helper scans eligible real staging directories, validates executable --version and selects an acceptable highest staged version. With !force, current C, staged S and reported latest L, S>=L causes staged_wins to select S. However the 'already staged' return is nested inside !is_newer(C,S). When C<S and S>=L, the function continues into preparation/activation instead of returning, so an already staged newer executable does not prevent duplicate work. Availability of a valid staged executable and successful validation are prerequisites; the audit did not create staging state or execute this branch (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/updates.rs:607-641; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/updates.rs:715-749).

The selected acquisition then goes through direct activation or the Windows detached helper. Temporary staging cleanup uses owned real-directory checks; successful Windows scheduling retains staging for the helper. Native comments that imply every newer staged version suppresses duplicate preparation must be corrected against this actual branch.
entries.interfaces: Native update [--force|-f] [--build] [--help|-h]; process-wide offline normalization; self-update staging and cached latest metadata; known target plus verified flag; CARGO_HOME and Rust wrapper environment checks. No TS --self/--extensions/--models target handling exists inside this native parser.
entries.dependency_text: Native cached metadata, executable validation/activation, prebuilt acquisition and Windows scheduling are prerequisites. TS command routing/explicit target sequencing is CLI-034/038 and is not counted again here.

The concrete gaps are the already-staged branch mismatch and an explicit target-version difference from TS: Cargo build installs the registry-selected current crate rather than passing the looked-up version. Fresh-cache fallback is visibly allowed for prebuilt target selection. All implementation and inline test bodies were read without running an updater.

Move/express the already-staged decision so a validated newer/equal-to-target pending update can suppress redundant preparation according to the intended policy, with force behavior explicit. Decide whether Cargo builds must use an exact checked version; if so pass it deliberately and handle forced/no-metadata builds separately. Keep cached-unverified metadata labeled as such and rely on verified artifact identity for acquisition. Estimated work covers those selection corrections and target integration, not rewriting activation. Future branch tests should cover C<S>=L, C=S, stale/invalid staging, force/build combinations and a looked-up version differing from Cargo's chosen version.

entries.title: Native executable activation safeguards and the post-collection output-cap defect
entries.what: Rust already verifies staged executable identity and performs guarded replacement with rollback. Its executable probe timeout is real, but the advertised output limit does not bound memory while the child is running.
entries.mechanism:
TS self-update delegates activation to an external package manager. Native activation validates both staged and destination files, replaces the executable through adjacent files and attempts rollback if post-replacement validation fails.

The direct plan requires a real nonempty regular current executable and owned real staging directory, creates unique adjacent new/old paths, and preflights replacement permissions with create_new probes. It validates staged --version, copies the staged executable, verifies byte equality/version, creates a hard-link backup of the current executable, checks that the destination has not changed and rejects a downgrade, then renames the replacement. Post-activation version/byte checks can trigger rollback through the backup; rollback failure is included in the returned error. Cleanup is best-effort. These are concrete preservation requirements, not a claim of crash-atomic multi-file state or universal platform support (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/updates.rs:1051-1266).

validate_ice_executable_version invokes the candidate with --version, requires successful exit and no stderr, and accepts one exact 'ice <semver>' line with at most its allowed terminal newline. It rejects extra lines/whitespace in the version and disallowed older versions. Downloaded release validation additionally compares the declared expected version. File validation rejects symlink leaf files/directories and checks canonical paths; it does not categorically reject every symlink in an ancestor path (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/updates.rs:877-895; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/updates.rs:1875-1985).

Source-proven bound defect: run_bounded_process_blocking launches a Tokio child with kill_on_drop and wraps wait_with_output in a 10-second timeout. Only after wait_with_output completes does cap_bytes truncate stdout and stderr to 4096 bytes each. Therefore the timeout limits waiting, and returned buffers are capped, but stdout/stderr can grow without that byte bound during collection. It is incorrect to call this a streaming memory cap. A child killed on timeout is not evidence of complete descendant-process cleanup (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/updates.rs:1781-1836).

The inline tests include malformed version output, file/path checks, byte mismatch, replacement failure and rollback fixtures. They were read only. No executable probe, replacement, crash simulation or platform-specific updater was run.
entries.interfaces: Staged/current executable paths, --version protocol, 10-second cooperative child timeout, 4096-byte retained stdout/stderr caps, unique adjacent replacement/backup files, exact expected release version for downloads. Activation returns a version or contextual failure including rollback outcome.
entries.dependency_text: This native validation primitive is used by self-update source selection, direct activation, prebuilt release validation and Windows staging. It does not depend on the TS package-manager command executor.
entries.rust: The direct replacement, version validation, leaf symlink rejection and rollback logic exist. The missing bound is during pipe ingestion: cap_bytes is called after full child output collection. Native safeguards are stronger than simply running an npm command, but that does not justify overstating the output limit or cleanup guarantee.
entries.port: Keep the native activation/rollback protocol. Replace wait_with_output's unbounded collection with concurrent bounded stdout/stderr readers and an explicit overflow policy, while preserving timeout, child reaping and exact version parsing. Reject overflow rather than accepting a silently truncated valid prefix as full protocol evidence. Define descendant cleanup separately if required. Future checks should cover output exceeding the cap before exit, independent stderr overflow, timeout while pipes remain open, valid first line followed by excess output, changed destination and failed rollback.
entries.priority_reason: A staged binary can consume unbounded probe memory before the current post-collection cap; activation must validate a complete bounded response.

entries.title: Native prebuilt CLI release verification and repository-case rejection defect
entries.what: Rust's default self-update path downloads a verified platform CLI executable. A mixed-case repository constant is compared against a lowercased canonical result, rejecting otherwise valid official release manifests before staging.
entries.mechanism:
TS self-update uses a checked npm package/version. Native prebuilt self-update instead fetches an ice-release.json manifest for the exact CLI release and verifies its archive and executable before activation.

The native manifest requires schema version 1, package name ice-cli, the requested semver, v<version> tag, the fixed official repository, a 40-character lower-case source commit, exact supported target and a flat platform binary name (ice or ice.exe). The archive must be zip/tar.gz with bounded positive size, matching SHA-256 and a release asset URL on the same repository/tag. It reuses the limited-body, safe extraction, hash and object-format validation helpers from prebuilt_extensions. Manifest fetch uses 15 seconds and archive fetch uses 180 seconds. The staged binary is create_new, synced and made executable on Unix, then its --version must match the requested version before activation (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/prebuilt_release.rs:1-189).

Source-proven fatal comparison: prebuilt_release::REPOSITORY is 'https://github.com/Zyk-Void/ice-rust'. validate compares canonical_repository(manifest.repository), which lowercases owner/repository, directly with that mixed-case constant. A matching official repository therefore becomes 'https://github.com/zyk-void/ice-rust' and cannot equal the constant. The rejection happens before archive staging. The release-asset URL validator also receives that mixed-case repository constant while comparing canonical repository strings, so fixing only the first comparison would leave the same class of mismatch at the URL boundary (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/prebuilt_release.rs:11; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/prebuilt_release.rs:50; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/prebuilt_release.rs:92; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/prebuilt_extensions.rs:158-195).

The happy-path inline fixture uses the same mixed-case official constant and expects staging to succeed; the visible transformations indicate it encounters the mismatch. This is a source-derived conclusion, not a reported test execution result. An ignored real-network smoke test exists and was not run. This defect is specific to the CLI prebuilt caller and does not invalidate all native extension prebuilt distribution, whose repository values are canonicalized through its own resolver.

Keep the exact manifest, hash, path, archive and executable checks after correcting repository identity. The default CLI update has no automatic Cargo fallback when the prebuilt protocol fails; users can separately select the build route.
entries.interfaces: GitHub release v<version>/ice-release.json; fixed official repository identity; schema 1 CLI release manifest; exact version/target/binary/archive/hash fields; --build as explicit alternative acquisition. The defect is independent of real network availability once the manifest has the expected official repository.
entries.dependency_text: CLI-041 owns shared canonical repository/archive/object helpers; CLI-044 owns staged executable --version validation. CLI-043 selects this acquisition path.
entries.rust: The complete protocol and tests are present in prebuilt_release.rs, but the canonicalized-lowercase versus mixed-case comparison makes the nominal official-manifest success path fail. This conclusion is bounded to the frozen source and visible helper behavior. It was not reproduced with a download or application command, and no upstream fix is assumed.
entries.port: Canonicalize both expected and supplied repository identities through one representation, or store the official constant in the helper's canonical form and use it consistently for manifest and asset URL checks. Preserve original casing only for display/URL construction where harmless. Recheck the existing positive fixture and negative publisher/tag/path cases in future implementation verification. Do not add a silent unverified fallback or loosen identity validation. The estimate covers the small comparison correction and consistent callers, not rebuilding the release pipeline.
entries.priority_reason: The default native prebuilt CLI update path rejects valid official release metadata before download/staging.

entries.title: Windows detached native activation, status consumption and timestamp-schema mismatch
entries.what: Native Windows update schedules a detached helper that waits for the current executable to exit and then replaces it with rollback support. Helper-written status timestamps use a different schema from the Rust consumer, so age-based cleanup does not work for those statuses.
entries.mechanism:
TS Windows npm self-update quarantines loaded dependency files before invoking its package manager. Rust has a separate executable activation helper that retains staging until the parent process exits.

The Rust path stages and validates the new executable, builds replacement/backup/status paths and writes preparing/scheduled status. It locates PowerShell through GetWindowsDirectoryW and the fixed System32 WindowsPowerShell executable, validates its MZ file header and never searches PATH. The helper command uses structured arguments with no profile, noninteractive mode, a system-only PSModulePath, null stdio and CREATE_NO_WINDOW. Successful spawn returns while the helper waits, retaining the staging directory and printing its status path (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/updates.rs:1549-1779; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/updates.rs:2284-2403).

The embedded helper validates paths, hashes and PE marker, verifies that the given parent PID belongs to the expected target executable, and waits up to 600000 ms. After the parent exits it rehashes staged content, copies/verifies it and uses File.Replace with backup. Post-replacement hash failure invokes the backup/displaced-file recovery paths and records failure including rollback details. Success/failure cleanup removes owned staged files and empty directories best-effort. It does not claim that returning from the Rust command means activation already happened (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/updates.rs:1295-1546).

Status consumption accepts bounded regular status files under the owned update root, with 32-hex status names and a 64 KiB read bound. Messages have control/whitespace normalized and are bounded to the implementation's 2048-character accumulation target. Failed statuses become warnings and are consumed independently of age; success statuses normally expire after 24 hours, nonterminal statuses after one hour, but age checks require updatedAtMs>0. Separate pruning handles eligible unclaimed pending staging directories: empty directories can be removed immediately, while payload/age/obsolete rules protect live work. Unknown-age status data is not assumed stale (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/updates.rs:1986-2283).

Source-proven schema defect: Rust SelfUpdateStatus deserializes camel-case updatedAtMs as a numeric value with default zero, and write_windows_update_status emits that field. The embedded PowerShell Write-UpdateStatus emits ISO-string updatedAt instead and replaces the status file. Helper waiting/succeeded statuses therefore read back with updatedAtMs=0, so the one-hour/24-hour TTL branches do not age them out as intended. Failed-status handling and independent orphan/empty staging cleanup can still run. Inline TTL fixtures manually supply updatedAtMs, so they do not establish the real helper output schema works (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/updates.rs:99-119; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/updates.rs:1310-1330; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/updates.rs:2119-2155; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/updates.rs:2391-2403).

All helper text and inline Windows/status tests were read without executing PowerShell, creating status files or replacing an executable. The TS loaded-DLL quarantine algorithm is MISC-002 and remains a separate runtime-specific mechanism.
entries.interfaces: Detached helper arguments include parent PID, staged/target/replacement/backup/status paths and expected hashes; status fields state, message, updatedAtMs (Rust) versus updatedAt (current helper). Limits: parent wait 600000 ms, status 64 KiB, nonterminal TTL one hour, success TTL 24 hours. Success scheduling and completed activation are distinct states.
entries.dependency_text: CLI-044 supplies staged executable/path/version validation. MISC-002 describes TS dependency quarantine and is only a comparison, not an implementation prerequisite for native executable replacement.
entries.rust: The detached helper, fixed PowerShell path, verified parent wait, hash checks, replacement/rollback and bounded status reads exist. The concrete missing compatibility is internal writer/reader timestamp agreement, not the whole Windows updater. The native helper's ISO updatedAt is ignored by the Rust updatedAtMs consumer; no OS execution was performed to claim end-to-end success.
entries.port: Keep the guarded detached activation workflow. Make helper and Rust writers share one timestamp field/type, preferably epoch milliseconds, and decide how to read already-written ISO statuses without treating unknown times as immediately expired. Exercise the actual helper-generated schema in future source/fixture verification rather than only hand-authored Rust records. Preserve failed warning consumption and staging ownership checks, and report scheduled versus activated state accurately. Estimated changes cover schema/cleanup correction, not replacement of the Windows activation mechanism.
entries.priority_reason: Real helper statuses bypass intended age cleanup because their timestamp field is not read, leaving stale pending/success state.
